title: Docker Compose Basics
subtitle: Define and run multi-container applications with a single YAML file

content.text: Running a modern application typically means running several containers together: an API server, a database, a cache, a message queue. Typing five docker run commands with all their flags is tedious, error-prone, and impossible to share. Docker Compose lets you define your entire multi-service stack in a single docker-compose.yml file, then start everything with one command: docker compose up.

content.code:
# docker-compose.yml — a full-stack web app: API + PostgreSQL + Redis
services:

  # ── API server ────────────────────────────────────────────
  api:
    build: .                        # build from Dockerfile in current dir
    image: myapp-api:dev            # name the built image
    container_name: myapp-api
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"                  # host:container
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: development
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:secret@postgres:5432/myapp
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379
    env_file:
      - .env.local                  # override with local env file
    volumes:
      - ./src:/app/src               # bind mount for hot reload
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy   # wait until postgres passes healthcheck
      redis:
        condition: service_started
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ── PostgreSQL database ───────────────────────────────────
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: myapp-postgres
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
      POSTGRES_DB: myapp
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data  # named volume — data persists
      - ./init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql  # auto-run on first start
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ── Redis cache ───────────────────────────────────────────
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: myapp-redis
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped

# Named volumes (persists data across compose down/up)
volumes:
  postgres-data:
  redis-data:

# Start all services (in background)
docker compose up -d

# Start and rebuild images (after Dockerfile changes)
docker compose up -d --build

# Start specific services only
docker compose up -d api redis

# Stop all services (containers stop, data preserved)
docker compose down

# Stop AND delete volumes (nuclear — deletes all data!)
docker compose down -v

# View logs for all services
docker compose logs -f

# View logs for a specific service
docker compose logs -f api

# Open a shell in a running service
docker compose exec api sh
docker compose exec postgres psql -U postgres myapp

# List running services
docker compose ps

# Run a one-off command in a service
docker compose run --rm api npm run migrate

content.text: docker compose vs docker-compose: The old standalone docker-compose (v1, Python) is deprecated. Use docker compose (space, no hyphen) — the v2 plugin built into Docker CLI. It's faster, has better error messages, and supports the latest features.

questions.question: Your API service has 'depends_on: postgres'. You run docker compose up. What does this guarantee?
options: The API will not start until PostgreSQL is fully ready to accept connections
Docker starts postgres before api, but does NOT wait for PostgreSQL to be ready — the API may still fail to connect if PG is slow to start
The API service will retry connecting to postgres until it succeeds
Docker Compose won't start at all until postgres is healthy
questions.explanation: By default, depends_on only controls START ORDER — not readiness. Docker starts postgres first, then api, but if PostgreSQL takes 3 seconds to initialize, the API might crash. To wait for readiness, use 'depends_on: condition: service_healthy' with a healthcheck defined on the postgres service.

faq.q: How do services reach each other in Compose?
faq.a: Docker Compose automatically creates a custom network for all services and makes each service reachable by its service name as a hostname. In the example above, the api service reaches PostgreSQL at 'postgres:5432' — no network: config needed. This is one of Compose's biggest conveniences.

examples: Most open-source projects ship a docker-compose.yml so contributors can run the full stack in one command — no manual database setup
CI pipelines use 'docker compose up -d' to spin up dependencies (postgres, redis, elasticsearch) before running integration tests
